posts.topic: How to sew a dart: mark, fold, stitch to a point

slides.title: How to sew a neat dart in 3 steps
slides.subtitle: Darts turn flat fabric into a shape that follows your body. Here's how to sew them without puckers.

slides.title: Transfer the markings
slides.body: Mark the dart legs and the point on the wrong side of the fabric with chalk or a fabric pen. Use a ruler to join the dots into two straight lines.

slides.title: Fold and pin
slides.body: Fold the fabric right sides together so the two lines sit exactly on top of each other. Pin across the lines, with the heads towards the edge.

slides.title: Stitch off the point
slides.body: Sew from the wide end towards the point, with the last few stitches right on the fold. Leave long threads and tie a knot instead of backstitching.

slides.title: Save this for sewing day
slides.body: Our patterns mark every dart clearly and walk you through each step, so shaping feels easy.

posts.caption_ig:
Darts look tricky, but they're just a fold sewn into a point 🪡

Swipe for the 3 steps: transfer the markings, fold and pin, then stitch off the point.

The secret to no puckers? Let the last few stitches run right along the fold, then tie off the threads instead of backstitching.

posts.topic: Match your machine needle to your fabric

slides.title: Pick the right needle for your fabric
slides.body: Use a ballpoint or jersey needle for knits, a universal needle for everyday cottons and a fine sharp needle for silky fabrics. Skipped stitches? Try a fresh needle first.

posts.caption_ig:
Skipped stitches, snags or little holes in your fabric? The needle might be the problem, not you 🧵

Knits like jersey and sweatshirt fleece love a ballpoint or jersey needle. Everyday cottons are happy with a universal. Silky, fine fabrics need a sharp, fine needle.

And if your stitches suddenly misbehave, swap in a fresh needle before anything else ✨

When did you last change yours? Be honest 😅

posts.topic: Testing your size with a toile (muslin)

slides.title: Test your size with a quick toile
slides.subtitle: Picked your size from the XS–XL chart? A practice version shows you the fit before you cut your good fabric.

slides.title: Use inexpensive fabric
slides.body: Cut the main pieces from calico, an old sheet or cheap fabric with a similar weight and stretch to your final fabric. Skip facings, pockets and linings.

slides.title: Sew the main seams
slides.body: Use a long stitch so it's easy to unpick. Sew the shoulders, side seams and darts, and baste in a zip or pin the opening closed.

slides.title: Try it on and mark
slides.body: Check the bust, waist, hip and length in front of a mirror. Pin out extra fabric or note where it pulls, then copy the changes onto your pattern.

slides.title: Sew it once, fit it right
slides.body: Every pattern comes in sizes XS–XL with US and UK sizing, so your toile starts close.

posts.caption_ig:
Nervous about cutting into that beautiful fabric? Make a toile first 🪡
